title: Why “boy" culture is creating a crisis of connection, with Niobe Way, PhD

sentences.en: Many boys form deep friendships in childhood, but as they become teens, something changes.
sentences.zh: 许多男孩在童年时期会建立深厚的友谊，但随着他们进入青春期，情况发生了一些变化。

sentences.en: They become more reluctant to open up to others and report fewer close, rich friendships.
sentences.zh: 他们变得更不愿向他人敞开心扉，报告的亲密、深厚的友谊也随之减少。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk to a psychologist who has spent decades studying boys' friendships
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将采访一位心理学家，她花了数十年时间研究男孩的友谊

sentences.en: and emotional development about why that happens and what it means for boys and men and for everyone else.
sentences.zh: 以及情感发展，探讨这种现象发生的原因，以及它对男孩、男人乃至所有人意味着什么。

sentences.en: What do boys learn about masculinity through their childhood and teen years?
sentences.zh: 男孩在童年和青春期通过什么来了解男子气概？

sentences.en: How do those lessons affect their mental health and relationships as they grow up?
sentences.zh: 这些经验如何影响他们成年后的心理健康和人际关系？

sentences.en: How do the norms and ideals of boy culture affect women and girls as well?
sentences.zh: 男孩文化的规范和理想又是如何影响女性和女孩的？

sentences.en: And what can parents and educators do to help us all stay emotionally connected to ourselves and each other?
sentences.zh: 家长和教育工作者能做些什么，来帮助我们所有人保持与自我及彼此的情感联结？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，

sentences.en: Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Niobe Wei, a professor of developmental psychology and director of the Science of Human Connection Lab at New York University.
sentences.zh: 今天我的嘉宾是纽约大学发展心理学教授、人类联结科学实验室主任尼奥比·韦博士。

sentences.en: Her work focuses on how culture shapes child development, especially in boys and young men, and how to foster connection and combat loneliness.
sentences.zh: 她的研究重点是文化如何塑造儿童发展，尤其是男孩和年轻男性的发展，以及如何促进联结和对抗孤独。

sentences.en: She's the author of more than 100 academic articles and books.
sentences.zh: 她撰写了100多篇学术文章和书籍。

sentences.en: Her newest book is Rebels with a Cause, Reimagining Boys, Ourselves, and Our Culture.
sentences.zh: 她的最新著作是《叛逆有理：重构男孩、我们自己与我们的文化》。

sentences.en: Her previous book,
sentences.zh: 她之前的著作，

sentences.en: Deep Secrets, Boys' Friendships and the Crisis of Connection, was the inspiration for the Oscar nominated movie, Close.
sentences.zh: 《深层秘密：男孩的友谊与联结危机》，是奥斯卡提名电影《亲密》的灵感来源。

sentences.en: Dr. Wei, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 韦博士，感谢您今天参加节目。

sentences.en: Oh, I'm so delighted to be here and thank you for the invitation.
sentences.zh: 哦，我很高兴能来到这里，谢谢您的邀请。

sentences.en: In your latest book and in your research, you talk about boy culture.
sentences.zh: 在您的最新著作和研究中，您谈到了“男孩文化”。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that term?
sentences.zh: 您所说的这个词是什么意思？

sentences.en: What is boy culture?
sentences.zh: 什么是男孩文化？

sentences.en: Well, this is an interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: So boy culture, and I want to make it very clear to your listeners that boy is in quotation, not boy culture, meaning it's a stereotype of a boy.
sentences.zh: 关于“男孩文化”，我想向听众明确一点，这里的“男孩”是加了引号的，它不是指真正的男孩，而是指一种关于男孩的刻板印象。

sentences.en: It's not a real boy.
sentences.zh: 它不是真实的男孩。

sentences.en: And the important part of this is what I'm about to say is it's taught to us by real boys.
sentences.zh: 这一点很重要，我要说的是，这种文化是由真实的男孩传授给我们的。

sentences.en: So real boys tell us how we've stereotyped boys in a way that's not only damaging them, but in some cases killing them.
sentences.zh: 真实的男孩告诉我们，我们对男孩的刻板印象不仅在伤害他们，在某些情况下甚至是在摧毁他们。

sentences.en: And so I want to be very dramatic about it because the results are very dramatic.
sentences.zh: 我想用词严厉一些，因为后果确实非常严重。

sentences.en: And so boy culture is essentially a culture that aligns with the stereotype of a boy that only values their hard side.
sentences.zh: 所以，男孩文化本质上是一种符合男孩刻板印象的文化，它只看重男孩“坚硬”的一面。

sentences.en: So only wants autonomy, doesn't care about connection, only wants to be stoic, doesn't care about their own vulnerabilities, doesn't even have the capacity
sentences.zh: 它只追求自主，不关心联结，只要求坚忍，不关心自己的脆弱，甚至没有能力

sentences.en: to be vulnerable, that doesn't have the soft skills that so-called girls and women have.
sentences.zh: 去表现脆弱，它缺乏所谓的女孩和女性所拥有的软技能。

sentences.en: They just have their hard skills.
sentences.zh: 他们只有所谓的“硬技能”。

sentences.en: And in fact, their soft skills, they're sort of, you know, emotionally and relationally unintelligent compared to girls and women.
sentences.zh: 事实上，与女孩和女性相比，他们的软技能，也就是情感和人际交往能力，被认为是不够聪明的。

sentences.en: That's all part of a stereotype of a boy that according to my almost 40 years of research with young people, and it's been all gender identities, but the point is that the boys and
sentences.zh: 这都是男孩刻板印象的一部分。根据我近40年来对年轻人的研究——涵盖了所有性别认同——关键在于，男孩和

sentences.en: young men are telling a story we're not listening to.
sentences.zh: 年轻男性正在讲述一个我们没有在倾听的故事。

sentences.en: What we learn from them is they not only have that intelligence, they have that intelligence as much as all other humans.
sentences.zh: 我们从他们身上学到的是，他们不仅拥有那种智慧，而且和其他人类一样拥有同等的智慧。

sentences.en: And the fact that we've stereotyped them as not being emotionally and relationally intelligent and not wanting emotionally
sentences.zh: 我们给他们贴上“情感和人际交往能力不足”以及“不需要情感

sentences.en: intimate friendships is what's damaging them, what's leading them to suicide and homicide and mass violence.
sentences.zh: 亲密友谊”的刻板印象，这正是伤害他们的根源，也是导致他们自杀、杀人及大规模暴力的原因。

sentences.en: And by the way, I just want to finally end with your response.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，最后我想用您的回应来结束这个话题。

sentences.en: The response, you learn that not only from boys in my research, boys and young men in my research, you learn it from the manifestos of mass shooters.
sentences.zh: 这个回应，您不仅能从我的研究对象——男孩和年轻男性身上学到，也能从大规模枪击案凶手的宣言中看到。

sentences.en: So they say the exact same thing.
sentences.zh: 他们说的是完全一样的话。

sentences.en: They're just more isolated kids.
sentences.zh: 他们只是更孤立的孩子。

sentences.en: So they end up committing violence.
sentences.zh: 所以他们最终诉诸暴力。

sentences.en: But the point is, it's the same story.
sentences.zh: 但重点是，故事是一样的。

sentences.en: And they've been telling this story to me since 1987, when I began to do research on social emotional development at Harvard as a grad student.
sentences.zh: 从1987年我作为哈佛研究生开始研究社会情感发展时起，他们就一直在向我讲述这个故事。

sentences.en: So what happens to boys' friendships as they move from childhood to adolescence?
sentences.zh: 那么，当男孩从童年步入青春期时，他们的友谊发生了什么变化？

sentences.en: Why do the ties seem to weaken them?
sentences.zh: 为什么这些纽带似乎削弱了他们？

sentences.en: And then what are the consequences for boys and young men?
sentences.zh: 这对男孩和年轻男性有什么后果？

sentences.zh: 金，我喜欢你的问题。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: They're really getting into you.
sentences.zh: 它们真的触及了核心。

sentences.en: Clearly read my book and it's beautiful to be asked these questions.
sentences.zh: 显然你读过我的书，被问到这些问题感觉真好。

sentences.en: So this is what happens.
sentences.zh: 事情是这样的。

sentences.en: And I report this in Deep Secrets, my previous book that was written about 13 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我在大约13年前写的上一本书《深层秘密》中报道过这一点。

sentences.en: What happens is, and boys, again, everything I say, I learned from listening to boys and young men.
sentences.zh: 发生的事情是——再次强调，我所说的一切都是通过倾听男孩和年轻男性的心声得来的。

sentences.en: So it's not my theory.
sentences.zh: 这不是我的理论。

sentences.en: It's not my, you know, it's my finding, but it's directly from the mouths of boys.
sentences.zh: 这不是我的……这是我的发现，但它直接出自男孩之口。

sentences.en: What happens as I'm a developmental psychologist, and for all the listeners, they know exactly what that is, which is
sentences.zh: 作为一名发展心理学家，对于所有听众来说，他们很清楚这意味着什么，

sentences.en: unusual for my audience, which is I follow the same kids over time.
sentences.zh: 这在我的受众中并不常见，那就是我长期追踪同一批孩子。

sentences.en: So I follow, you know, our teams have been following young people from the ages of 11, 12 to when, you know, following them all throughout
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的团队一直在追踪年轻人，从他们11、12岁开始，一直追踪到

sentences.en: So early, middle, and late adolescence.
sentences.zh: 也就是青春期的早期、中期和晚期。

sentences.en: And what we hear that that's the developmental work.
sentences.zh: 我们所听到的，就是这项发展研究的工作成果。

sentences.en: And I say this to all you wonderful APA members that get it.
sentences.zh: 我对所有理解这一点的优秀美国心理学会成员说：

sentences.en: It's the developmental work that tells the story about the impact of boy culture.
sentences.zh: 正是这项发展研究揭示了男孩文化的影响。

sentences.en: And I'll tell you why, because at 11, 12, and 13, boys are talking like all other humans.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你们原因，因为在11、12和13岁时，男孩的谈话方式和其他人类一样。

sentences.en: They're talking like girls, but it's not really like girls.
sentences.zh: 他们谈话的方式像女孩，但其实并不完全像女孩。

sentences.en: It's just like a human.
sentences.zh: 那只是像一个普通人。

sentences.en: They talk about their desire for connection.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论对联结的渴望。

sentences.en: They say things, if I wasn't, if they have close friendships, they say, if I didn't have him, him, I would, I would feel all alone.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，如果他们有亲密的友谊，他们会说：“如果没有他，我会感到非常孤独。”

sentences.en: I'd want to kill myself.
sentences.zh: “我会想自杀。”

sentences.en: They link it directly to mental health, their friendships directly to mental health.
sentences.zh: 他们直接将友谊与心理健康联系起来。

sentences.en: They reveal their, and this gives me the chills every time I talk about it.
sentences.zh: 他们展现出的……每次谈到这个，我都会起鸡皮疙瘩。

sentences.en: It's so beautiful.
sentences.zh: 这太美好了。

sentences.en: They reveal their relational intelligence, their capacity to look at the human world and understand that underneath anger is always hurt feelings.
sentences.zh: 他们展现了他们的人际智慧，他们有能力审视人类世界，并理解愤怒之下总是隐藏着受伤的感情。

sentences.en: They say that directly.
sentences.zh: 他们直接这样说。

sentences.en: You know, I may be, I may be pissed at you, but it's really that I feel like you dissed me and it hurts my feelings.
sentences.zh: “你知道，我可能在生你的气，但实际上是因为我觉得你轻视了我，这伤害了我的感情。”

sentences.en: You know, they get it.
sentences.zh: 你看，他们懂的。

sentences.en: They have this extraordinary relational intelligence of getting the human world and the contradictions and the way we fake
sentences.zh: 他们拥有非凡的人际智慧，能够理解人类世界、矛盾以及我们伪装

sentences.en: emotions and all those kinds of things to try to, you know, and they don't understand why we would ask them to do anything else, but be a human.
sentences.zh: 情绪的方式等等。他们不明白为什么我们要求他们做别的，而不是做一个真实的人。

sentences.en: And then as they get older and the pressure is to man up, and this is the critical thing for a psychologist, not only to man up, but to mature
sentences.zh: 然后，随着他们长大，压力要求他们“像个男人”，这对心理学家来说是关键点，不仅要“像个男人”，还要成熟，

sentences.en: Kim, to become a grownup.
sentences.zh: 金，要成为一个成年人。

sentences.en: We ask them to basically take their soft skills, their soft, so-called soft needs.
sentences.zh: 我们要求他们基本上把他们的软技能，他们所谓的软需求——

sentences.en: It's not a gender identity.
sentences.zh: 这不是性别认同，

sentences.en: It's a human need, but we gender it as feminine and soft.
sentences.zh: 这是人类的需求，但我们将其性别化为女性化和软弱。

sentences.en: We tell them to go underground with that.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉他们要把这些需求隐藏起来。

sentences.en: In fact, those skills are not really important and they're not really something that we value.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些技能并不重要，也不是我们所看重的。

sentences.en: And I can tell you why we, I know that is because we value cognitive intelligence.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你为什么，因为我们看重的是认知智能。

sentences.en: We don't value emotional intelligence and relational intelligence the same way.
sentences.zh: 我们不像看重认知智能那样看重情感智能和人际智能。

sentences.en: So boys get these messages about manhood and maturity, you know, to focus on separation rather than connection, right?
sentences.zh: 所以男孩们接收到关于男子气概和成熟的信息，你知道，要专注于分离而不是联结，对吧？

sentences.en: Autonomy, independence over interdependence.
sentences.zh: 自主和独立高于相互依赖。

sentences.en: We, you know, boys are getting that.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，男孩们接收到了这些信息。

sentences.en: Of course, everybody's getting that, but boys are getting it profoundly because it's also linked to masculinity.
sentences.zh: 当然，每个人都在接收这些信息，但男孩们感受得尤为深刻，因为它还与男子气概挂钩。

sentences.en: And then they start to disconnect.
sentences.zh: 然后他们开始断联。

sentences.en: This is answering now, answering your question.
sentences.zh: 现在我来回答你的问题。

sentences.en: They start to disconnect from what they want and what they need, which is their friendships.
sentences.zh: 他们开始与自己想要的和需要的——也就是他们的友谊——断联。

sentences.en: So they start to go under, you literally hear it in their language.
sentences.zh: 所以他们开始压抑，你甚至能从他们的语言中听出来。

sentences.en: It's incredible.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: Their language that was soft and beautiful and emotional in early to middle adolescence starts to sound like a stereotypic guy.
sentences.zh: 他们在青春期早期到中期那种柔软、美丽且充满情感的语言，开始变得像刻板印象中的男人。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: “无所谓。”

sentences.zh: “一切都好。”

sentences.zh: “一切都好。”

sentences.en: I don't need friends or, or if I, you know, the more tender boys that are willing to still be tender, they'll say things like, um, I, you know, I, I struggled to hold onto my
sentences.zh: “我不需要朋友。”或者，如果那些更温柔、依然愿意保持温柔的男孩，他们会说：“我努力想维持我的

sentences.en: friendships.
sentences.zh: 友谊。”

sentences.zh: “这很悲伤，因为我曾经拥有这些友谊。”

sentences.zh: “我现在没有了。”

sentences.en: Um, and then, and then some of them, this is what's the most amazing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后，最令人惊奇的是，

sentences.en: They name boy culture.
sentences.zh: 他们指出了“男孩文化”。

sentences.en: They say things like, it might be nice to be a girl.
sentences.zh: 他们会说：“如果我是个女孩就好了。”

sentences.en: Cause then I wouldn't have to be emotionless.
sentences.zh: “因为那样我就不必表现得毫无感情。”

sentences.en: I mean, they name it or they say, you know, uh, I'm, I'm grown up now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们指出了这一点，或者他们说：“你知道，我已经长大了。”

sentences.en: I'm, you know, I've matured enough.

sentences.zh: “我不需要分享我的感受。”

sentences.en: I mean, Kim, I mean, that's, it's not, you know, what I want to communicate to our listeners, especially the APA community.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，金，我想向我们的听众，特别是美国心理学会的社区传达的是，

sentences.en: It's not, this is not a theory that I'm coming up with about boy culture and boys.
sentences.zh: 这并不是我关于男孩文化和男孩所提出的理论。

sentences.en: This is told directly from the mouths of babes.
sentences.zh: 这是直接出自孩子们的口中。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Like they're saying it directly that growing up in a culture that only values my hard side and doesn't value my soft side, my soft capacities actually causes me to feel
sentences.zh: 他们直接说，在一个只看重我坚硬一面、不看重我柔软一面和柔软能力的文化中成长，实际上让我对自己感觉

sentences.en: terrible about myself and oftentimes feel terrible about others.
sentences.zh: 很糟糕，而且往往对他人也感觉很糟糕。

sentences.en: Um, and so the idea is we need our hard and soft.

sentences.en: That's our first mistake.

sentences.zh: 我们在发展理论中已经谈论了很久，但重点是鲍尔比是对的。

sentences.en: And then what we, I say in my new book, rebels, it actually harms all of us because now you get girls and I have to say this girls are emphasizing manning up as two as well.

sentences.en: and I was working in public schools in Boston, that oftentimes the stories you would get, you know, even deep secrets that was written off based on in part, my studies in Boston,

sentences.en: They don't see the way, you know, the, the way they've been damaged by boy culture too, by the way, they don't see it.

sentences.en: By, you know, all sorts of divisions we have, they're much more willing to speak truth to power.

sentences.en: So the idea is that to me, the working class young people and the kids of color, and I want to say this to all psychologists, they oftentimes tell us

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.en: I mean, I mean, my father said, I want to end with one, I mean, end of the response with one more insight from my father.

sentences.en: Actually, he said, when I was 18, I was interested in American adolescents.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他说，当我18岁时，我对美国青少年很感兴趣。

sentences.en: I've always been interested in American adolescents.
sentences.zh: 我一直对美国青少年很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And he said, Niobe, if you're interested in American adolescents, go live in China.
sentences.zh: 他说，尼奥比，如果你对美国青少年感兴趣，那就去中国住住。

sentences.en: And his point was, you can't see yourself if you only see yourself, right?
sentences.zh: 他的意思是，如果你只看你自己，你就看不见你自己，对吧？

sentences.zh: 你必须去看点什么，看某个人，对吧？

sentences.en: And, and psychologists, I'm going to, I'm going to, I'm going to critique the field of psychology in some ways, especially research

sentences.en: We do that sort of matching thing.

sentences.en: And who don't have the same background.
sentences.zh: 以及那些背景与我不同的人。

sentences.en: And so to me, I do, it's an important point in psychology.

sentences.en: The studies of kids of color and from working class families are not just studies of kids of color and working class families.

sentences.en: They are studies of humans and what it means to be human and what's getting in the way of our capacity to be human.

sentences.en: And I want us to shift that in the field so that we understand that including women, right, as Carol Gilligan said decades ago, is not just about women, it's about being human.

sentences.en: It's a human voice.

sentences.en: And we're building it with an app we're building now called Agapi that we've been working with teenagers for the last year every week to co-design it.
sentences.zh: 我们正在用一款名为Agapi的应用程序来构建它，在过去的一年里，我们每周都与青少年合作共同设计它。

sentences.en: We're coming out with an MVP of the app in
sentences.zh: 我们将在

sentences.en: August that basically nurtures friendships and bridges divides by using my practices of listening with curiosity and we gamify it.
sentences.zh: 八月推出该应用程序的最小可行性产品（MVP），它基本上通过使用我“带着好奇心倾听”的实践来培养友谊并弥合分歧，并且我们将它游戏化了。

sentences.en: So it's fun and engaging and kids get listening points and all sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 所以它很有趣且引人入胜，孩子们可以获得倾听积分和各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: But it's a fun thing to do.
sentences.zh: 但这是一件有趣的事情。

sentences.en: But teenagers have helped us create it so made sure it stays fun.
sentences.zh: 但青少年帮助我们创造了它，所以确保了它保持趣味性。

sentences.en: But the point is we need to create a pro-social culture and there's lots of ways of doing it in your homes, in your schools, through technology, right?
sentences.zh: 但重点是我们确实需要创造一种亲社会文化，在你的家庭、学校、通过技术，有很多方法可以做到这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: We just need to recognize the problem, Kim, is an anti-social culture and thus the solution, right, is a pro-social culture.
sentences.zh: 我们只需要认识到问题，金，在于反社会文化，因此解决方案，对吧，就是亲社会文化。

sentences.en: If we're social by nature, which we are, then our anti-social culture, it's a culture-nature clash.
sentences.zh: 如果我们天生是社会性的，事实确实如此，那么我们的反社会文化就是一种文化与本性的冲突。

sentences.en: And the solution is to create a pro-social culture so that aligns better with our social nature.
sentences.zh: 而解决方案就是创造一种亲社会文化，使其与我们的社会本性更好地契合。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Wei, this has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 好的，魏博士，这真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: I think your work is quite important and I'm going to stay tuned to see what comes next.
sentences.zh: 我认为你的工作非常重要，我会持续关注接下来的进展。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me.
sentences.zh: 感谢你参加我的节目。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢。
